Unlabelled, the agent stage falls back to citing paragraph numbers — and a bullet
list is one paragraph, so seven criteria collapse into a single citation meaning
"somewhere in the seven". Labels also survive editing; a paragraph index does
not.

**6. Check it carries enough for the next stage.** `agent-work-item` prepares the
same item for an autonomous agent. It needs things it cannot invent:

- a goal stating what is true when the work is done
- the problem, and why now
- a number wherever a requirement depends on one; a sentence that only motivates
  the work needs none
- what must keep working, not only what must change
- what is out of scope
- a name against every open question
- no two criteria that need an unstated fact to reconcile

Anything missing is a finding. Take it back through step 4. Do not write the
agent's artifact here — different skill, different structure.

The last one exists because this list and the agent stage's own gate were not the
same test. An item passed this check and was then refused there, over two criteria
that only agree if you already know something the item never says. Whatever you
settled in step 4 has to be readable off the page, or the next stage either stops
or invents it.

**7. Run the six lenses again over the rewrite.** A rewrite creates new gaps: a
requirement you changed in step 5 can leave a criterion that no longer matches
it. This is a full second pass, not a re-read for typos.

**Read it as someone who was not in the conversation.** You know what you meant,
which is exactly what disqualifies you from reading it. An inference you drew is
not in the text unless you wrote it there, and a conflict you settled in your head
is still a conflict on the page.

The `conflict` lens is where this bites. Two criteria on a real item read as
agreeing only if you already knew the decision behind them; the author re-read
them and saw agreement, and the next stage saw a contradiction and stopped.

**8. Show the rewritten item and wait for approval.** Approval gates the record —
the tracker, the repository, any commit. It does not gate your working notes. Keep
a local draft per attempt, including the ones that were rejected; a later reader
can only see what changed by reading them side by side.

**9. Write the run out where it can be re-read.** If a `docs/passes/` directory
exists, find the highest-numbered `passN` inside it and write your findings and
the item you were given there. Elsewhere, do nothing — the directory belongs to
the repository you are in, not to this skill.

## An item returned from the agent stage

`agent-work-item` refuses an item it cannot derive obligations from, and writes one
blocker per missing thing onto the item. An item arriving that way is not a raw
item, and the procedure above is the wrong one for it.

**Resolve what the blockers name. Nothing else.**

- Do not re-run the six lenses. That text has been through them, and a full pass
  over a refined item produces findings nobody asked for: one real run produced
  nine on an item that needed one sentence.
- Take one blocker at a time, by the rules in step 4. A contradiction gets 2-4
  readings; something the item never said gets stated and asked.
- Write the answer into the item, not into your reply. The gate refused because
  the text did not say it, so a text that still does not say it is refused again.
- Then run step 7 over what you changed, and only what you changed.

Clear every blocker or clear none. A partly answered refusal fails the gate on the
same condition it failed before, which is a conversation rather than another round.

## When it is done

Not when you run out of findings. Done is when a fresh reader can say all five of
these, and has no blocking question left:

- what the item wants
- what would make it done
- what must keep working
- what is out of scope
- what is still unanswered, and who answers it

Questions about how or where to build it do not block.

Stop at the first version that passes. Structure added past that point is cost
with no return.

An unanswered finding that was not blocking does not hold this open. A recorded
gap with a name against it is a finished part of the item, not an unfinished one.

1	# The refinement loop
2	
3	How modus's two skills and one boundary get improved together.
4	
5	`docs/plugin-evaluation.md` answers whether a skill fires. This answers something
6	one level up: whether the three artifacts in a chain are good enough, when each
7	one's ceiling is set by the artifact before it.
8	
9	## Why the three cannot be improved separately
10	
11	The chain is:
12	
13	```
14	raw item
15	  → human-work-item    → a refined item a person can read
16	  → agent-work-item    → criteria an autonomous agent can work from
17	  → the drafter (#158) → the boundary
18	  → assessment         → defects
19	
20	        ^                             |
21	        |_____ blockers on the item __|
22	              agent-work-item refuses
23	```
24	
25	The back edge is the part that took eight passes to find. Some gaps in a human
26	item are only visible when something downstream tries to derive obligations from
27	it and finds it cannot — you do not know what you need until you need it. So the
28	chain is not one-way: `agent-work-item`'s gate writes one blocker per missing
29	thing onto the item, and `human-work-item` has a mode for an item that arrives
30	that way, which resolves what the blockers name and nothing else.
31	
32	That is the same mechanism #158 specifies for the drafter it describes. The
33	process building it gets what it is building.
34	
35	It terminates on a rule rather than on patience: a condition that fails the gate
36	twice means the answer did not land, and that is a conversation with a person
37	rather than another lap.
38	
39	Today `agent-work-item` spans the last two arrows: a person follows the skill and
40	writes the boundary manifest by hand. The drafter is what #158 delivers, so the
41	final arrow is the deliverable rather than a stage the loop can run. The loop runs
42	the stages that exist.
43	
44	A refined item that never states what must keep working gives the stages below it
45	nothing to write a preservation entry from. The boundary is then missing that
46	entry, and the boundary is not what is wrong. Tuning `agent-work-item` against a
47	weak refined item measures the item, not the skill.
48	
49	So a pass runs the whole chain and the fixes land wherever the defect was
50	created.
51	
52	## The item under test
53	
54	GitHub #158, "Draft the boundary from the refined criteria". It is the goal and
55	the fixture at once: completing it requires running the process it describes.
56	Pass 3 rewrote its title and body, so the placeholder wording that pass 1 and 2
57	worked against is now only in `docs/passes/pass1/item.json`.
58	
59	The GitHub issue is the item of record. Beads are derivative — `domestique-3z5`
60	covers the same goal, and where the two disagree the issue wins. A reader outside
61	this repository can see the issue; bead ids are hash-suffixed and mean nothing to
62	them.
63	
64	### Where the item lives
65	
66	`docs/passes/passN/item.json` is the GitHub API response as fetched at the start
67	of pass N, stored verbatim rather than as pasted text. `agent-work-item` step 1
68	warns that a tracker's UI and its API can return different content for the same
69	item, and bead `domestique-2no` is open on it, so the fixture is what an adapter
70	actually receives.
71	
72	The item advances by design. A pass may write an improved item back to the issue,
73	and the next pass fetches it again — so the item converges alongside the skills.
74	This is the bootstrapping period and several changes are expected before the
75	drafter exists.
76	
77	There is one number, the pass number. An earlier version of this document kept a
78	separate generation count and the two did not line up: generations 1 and 2 both
79	came out of pass 3. The historical files are under `docs/passes/pass1/` and
80	`docs/passes/pass3/`, which is where they belong.
81	
82	`modus/evals/158-human-work-item/expected.md` records what was decided, who
83	decided it, the inferences drawn rather than asked, and the split proposed and not
84	made. It does not copy the item text — the pass directories hold that, and two
85	copies would drift.
86	
87	**An item is never at a fixed point while the skills are still changing.** What
88	converges is the pair, not the item. A better skill finds more on the same text,
89	so more findings after a skill edit is the expected result and is evidence the
90	edit worked.
91	
92	An earlier version of this document said the opposite — that a pass over an
93	unchanged item should find nothing. Pass 7 found nine findings on the text passes
94	4 to 6 had run against, because passes 4 and 5 had improved `human-work-item` in
95	between. The claim was wrong in its polarity: finding nothing is the exception.
96	
97	## How a pass runs
98	
99	Every pass writes into its own directory, so a pass can be re-read after the fact
100	and compared with the one before it.
101	
102	```
103	docs/passes/passN/
104	  item.json          the issue as fetched at the start of the pass
105	  stage1-*.txt       what human-work-item said about it
106	  stage2-*.txt       what agent-work-item said about it
107	  boundary.yaml      the boundary, where stage 2 produced one
108	  stage2-review.md   what step 8 found
109	  notes.md           this session's evaluation of the pass
110	```
111	
112	Both skills write there themselves, conditional on the directory existing. The
113	path is this repository's and not part of either plugin, so outside a checkout
114	with `docs/passes/` the instruction is inert.
115	
116	**1. Make the directory and fetch the item.**
117	
118	```bash
119	N=7; mkdir -p docs/passes/pass$N
120	gh issue view 158 --json number,url,title,state,body,labels,comments,author,createdAt,updatedAt \
121	  | python3 -m json.tool > docs/passes/pass$N/item.json
122	```
123	
124	The fetched item is the pass's input. There is no separate generation numbering —
125	one number, the pass number, and `docs/passes/passN/item.json` is what pass N ran
126	against.
127	
128	**2. Stage 1 — `human-work-item`. A check, not a gate.**
129	
130	```bash
131	node scripts/probe-skill.js --plugin modus --expect modus:human-work-item \
132	  --prompt "$(...)" --full > docs/passes/pass$N/stage1-human-work-item.txt
133	```
134	
135	It reports whether the current item still generates findings, and which of them
136	block. The pass continues either way. Runs in the neutral temporary directory,
137	because stage 1 reads the item and nothing else.
138	
139	The probe is one-shot and `human-work-item` stops after one question, so a probe
140	run reaches its findings and its first question and no further. As a check that
141	does not matter. It cannot complete a refinement, so do not plan a pass that
142	expects it to.
143	
144	**3. Stage 2 — `agent-work-item`. This one gates.**
145	
146	```bash
147	node scripts/probe-skill.js --plugin modus --expect modus:agent-work-item \
148	  --cwd "$(pwd)" --prompt "$(...)" --full > docs/passes/pass$N/stage2-agent-work-item.txt
149	```
150	
151	`--cwd` is required. Step 2 of that skill reads the repository to find what the
152	item does not say, and the probe's default temporary directory has nothing in it.
153	
154	No boundary can be produced without complete criteria from this stage, so this is
155	where a pass stops. Its own step 1b refuses an item missing an outcome, a
156	falsifiable criterion per obligation, what must keep working, or what is out of
157	scope — and says which is absent rather than drafting a partial boundary.
158	
159	**3b. Route every stage-1 finding.** Stage 1 does not gate, and that is not the
160	same as its output being advisory. Each finding goes to exactly one place, by the
161	attribution rule below:
162	
163	| | |
164	| --- | --- |
165	| the item is wrong or incomplete | fix the item, and the next pass fetches it |
166	| the skill missed it before and finds it now | nothing to fix — the skill edit worked |
167	| the skill should have found it and did not | fix the skill |
168	| nobody has decided it | record it, with a name against it |
169	
170	A finding left in a transcript is a finding nobody acts on. Pass 7 produced nine
171	and this step did not exist, so all nine sat in a file.
172	
173	**4. Evaluate the pass.** Read all of it and look for what is missing. Write the
174	result to `notes.md` in the pass directory, and add a row to the pass record at
175	the end of this document. This step is a person and a session, not a script.
176	
177	## The assessment
178	
179	One check, and it is the one `agent-work-item`'s own review questions do not ask.
180	
181	**Does the boundary name what the item does not.** The value is in the consumer,
182	the constant, or the missing test the item never mentions. A boundary that
183	restates the item in manifest form lints clean and saves nobody anything. This is
184	AC-9 in `boundary/agent-work-item-skill.yaml`.
185	
186	Two other checks used to live here — whether a fresh reader can state what must be
187	true, and whether every `decision` can be false. Both are already in the skill, as
188	step 9 and as one of step 8's two questions, so they were a second copy that could
189	drift. Run the skill's steps and read what step 8 returned.
190	
191	They were also declared to "run every pass", which was never true of any pass:
192	passes 1 to 5 never reached stage 2, and pass 6 was the first to produce a
193	boundary at all.
194	
195	## The attribution rule
196	
197	A defect in the boundary does not mean the boundary is what to fix.
198	
199	**Fix at the earliest stage whose output already contained the defect.**
200	
201	Read backwards from the defect:
202	
203	| The defect is already visible in | Fix |
204	| --- | --- |
205	| the raw item, and the refined item did not resolve it | `human-work-item` |
206	| the refined item, absent from the raw item | `human-work-item` |
207	| the boundary, absent from the refined item | `agent-work-item` |
208	| nothing upstream, and both skills were followed as written | the boundary draft |
209	| the raw item, and the human answered "not decided" | nothing — the item is a placeholder |
210	| the raw item, and the human says the item is wrong about its own subject | the item itself — a `contradicted` finding, which may change what gets built |
211	
212	Three consequences worth stating, because all three are easy to get wrong:
213	
214	- A defect present in the refined item **and** the boundary belongs to
215	  `human-work-item`. It will also look like an `agent-work-item` defect. It is
216	  not one.
217	- A skill that was not followed is not a skill defect until you have checked
218	  whether it *could* be followed. If the instruction was clear and got skipped,
219	  that is a compliance failure and the fix is bulletproofing, not new content.
220	  See `superpowers:writing-skills` on matching the form to the failure.
221	- A recorded open question is not a defect. A skill refusing to guess is the
222	  skill working. Attribute a defect only where a skill could have resolved
223	  something and did not.
224	
225	## The control item
226	
227	A second work item that runs through the flow every pass, and that the skills are
228	never edited because of. Its only job is to catch one failure: the skills getting
229	fitted to #158 instead of to work items in general.
230	
231	Without it, each pass adds instructions that happen to help #158. The skills
232	improve on #158 and get no better — possibly worse — on anything else. #158's own
233	results cannot show that, because #158 is improving the whole time.
234	
235	The item: the CSV export ticket in
236	`modus/evals/human-work-item-resolves-before-rewriting/prompt.md`. Synthetic,
237	written to carry one defect per lens.
238	
239	Read its result every pass. Change nothing on its account. If it degrades while
240	#158 improves, the last edit fitted #158.
241	
242	Once the item under test advances each pass, this is the only thing left holding
243	skill quality honest. A better boundary can come from a better item as easily as
244	from a better skill, and the attribution rule covers defects rather than
245	improvements. This item is not a precaution any more.
246	
247	**What this control item cannot detect.** It fails by contradiction and runs about
248	twice the length of a real issue here. The five open issues are 273 to 460
249	characters, carry a labelled Problem and Goal, and fail by omission instead. So
250	this item can show the skills being fitted to #158's subject. It cannot show them
251	being fitted to long contradictory tickets and losing the terse-omission case,
252	which is the failure this repository's own items actually have. Swapping in a
253	real issue — #156 is the furthest from #158 in subject — is the fix if that
254	becomes a live worry.
255	
256	## These passes are pre-freeze
257	
258	`agent-work-item` step 10 says a frozen boundary is the standard and is not
259	edited. This loop re-drafts the boundary every pass, so no boundary produced by a
260	pass is frozen. Each carries the marker:
261	
262	```
263	# NOT FROZEN. Pass N of the refinement loop.
264	```
265	
266	The freeze happens once, after the loop stops, on the boundary that a human
267	approves. Editing a frozen boundary because a later pass disagreed with it is the
268	failure modus exists to prevent.
269	
270	## Proposed and unresolved
271	
272	Proposals a pass makes and nobody has settled. Without this they are re-proposed
273	from scratch every pass, and the fact that they keep coming back is lost.
274	
275	| Proposal | Raised | State |
276	| --- | --- | --- |
277	| split #158 in two | pass 6 along AC3/AC4, pass 7 along AC6/AC7 | unresolved. Two passes proposed different lines, which is itself evidence the item holds more than one goal and that nobody can say where the seam is |
278	| make #156 the control item | pass 4 | unresolved. The synthetic export ticket is compromised for two behaviours after pass 4 drove edits from it |
279	| reduce the two human touchpoints | pass 3 | deferred by decision, blocked on measuring what review costs |
280	
281	A proposal that recurs with a different shape each time is not the same proposal
282	twice. It is a signal that the question is wrong, or that the item is too broad to
283	answer it.
284	
285	## When the loop stops
286	
287	Three conditions, and the third is the one that makes the other two mean
288	anything:
289	
290	- The boundary names what the item does not.
291	- The control item did not degrade.
292	- **Neither the skills nor the item changed since the previous pass, and stage 1
293	  still finds nothing new.**
294	
295	The third condition is why reaching a fixed point takes a deliberate act. While
296	skills keep improving, each pass finds more on the same item, and "more findings"
297	is indistinguishable from "the item got worse" if nothing was held still. Ending
298	the loop means choosing one pass in which nothing is edited, and seeing what a
299	frozen pair finds.
300	
301	An earlier version required "no change to either skill", which no pass can satisfy
302	while the loop is doing its job — the loop's whole design is that skills improve
303	every pass.
304	
305	## When the loop is blocked
306	
307	Not the same as stopping. The loop is blocked when every remaining open question
308	needs evidence nobody has. No number of passes closes it, and further passes
309	produce invented answers.
310	
311	**Try to unblock before declaring it.** An undecided question is not the only
312	thing standing in the way — the item's scope is also in play, and scope is
313	decidable today because it is a human's call rather than a measurement. See
314	Unblocking a placeholder in `human-work-item`: move the decision out of the item,
315	separate motivation from requirement, or replace the unmeasurable measure with an
316	observable one.
317	
318	Pass 1 declared #158 blocked on two questions. Pass 2 unblocked both without
319	answering either. Declaring blocked before trying those three moves costs a pass
320	and produces nothing.
321	
322	Blocked is still a real state and worth reporting when it holds. Name the
323	questions, name what would answer each, and hold the loop until that evidence
324	exists.
325	
326	## Pass record
327	
328	One row per pass, appended to this file.
329	
330	| Pass | Findings | Attributed to | Control item |
331	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
332	| 1 | 5 | `human-work-item` 4, this document 1 | unchanged |
333	| 2 | 4 | `human-work-item` 2, #158 itself 2 | unchanged |
334	| 3 | 8 | `human-work-item` 2, this document 4, #158 itself 2 | 8 findings against 10 |
335	| 4 | 3 | `human-work-item` 2, both skills 1 | **used to drive edits — see below** |
336	| 5 | 4 | `human-work-item` 4 | n/a — verified on #156 |
337	| 6 | 7 | `agent-work-item` 1, `lint-boundary.js` 1, the draft 5 | not re-run |
338	
339	### Pass 1
340	
341	Stage 1 only. #158 is a placeholder: the human's role once the feature ships, and
342	the number that decides "scales", are both undecided rather than unwritten.
343	Stages 2 and 3 did not run.
344	
345	Findings against `human-work-item`:
346	
347	1. Step 4 gave a form for conflicts only. With no form for a missing
348	   requirement, the run offered the human a menu of invented answers — and named
349	   a linter, a manifest schema and a fixture corpus inside it, which is
350	   implementation inside a question about the WHAT.
351	2. No red flag against offering that menu.
352	3. The wording rules banned metaphor but not unexplained vocabulary, so
353	   "preservation obligation" and "held-out item" reached the human unexplained.
354	4. No notion of a placeholder. The skill assumed refinement throughout, and its
355	   Out of scope excluded "creating a work item from nothing" — excluding its own
356	   common case.
357	
358	Finding against this document: the attribution table had no row for an answer of
359	"not decided", so a correctly recorded open question read as a `human-work-item`
360	defect. Fixed above.
361	
362	All five are fixed.
363	
364	### Pass 2
365	
366	Stage 1. #158 was unblocked without answering either question from pass 1, using
367	two of the three moves in Unblocking a placeholder: the human-involvement
368	decision moved out of the item into a separate one, and "doesn't scale" was
369	reclassified from requirement to motivation. The measure was then replaced with
370	an observable one — a reviewer names no entry they had to write themselves.
371	
372	#158 is defined and awaiting approval. It does not reach `expected.md` until then.
373	
374	Findings against `human-work-item`, both fixed:
375	
376	1. "Wait for approval before writing it anywhere" banned the per-pass working
377	   draft this document requires, so a rejected draft would never be written and
378	   the comparison would be lost. Step 8 now gates the record rather than the
379	   notes.
380	2. The acceptance-criteria test said a bullet needing judgment fails but named no
381	   forms, and a draft bullet used "approves" — which `boundary-prose.md` rejects
382	   as a state of mind. The three failing forms are now named with replacements.
383	
384	Findings against #158, carried to its open questions rather than fixed here:
385	
386	- A recorded blocker is not required to name what is wrong. A blocker reading
387	  "rejected" cannot be resolved.
388	- No outcome after a blocker is resolved: whether drafting resumes on its own or
389	  has to be re-requested.
390	
391	Both came out of step 7, the second lens pass over the rewrite, on the first item
392	that step has ever run against.
393	
394	### Pass 3
395	
396	Complete. #158 was rewritten and approved, and the title and body were written
397	back to the issue. The fixture was re-captured as generation 1 and generation 0
398	kept. Generation 2 followed, adding citation labels without changing wording.
399	
400	Both skills learned the label scheme. `human-work-item` step 5 labels every
401	separately falsifiable claim; `agent-work-item` step 1 cites a label where the
402	item carries one and falls back to `<field>#<n>` where it does not. The fallback
403	matters — #156, #157 and the control item carry no labels and still work.
404	
405	The label change came from a defect the definition itself created. Generation 1
406	put seven criteria in one bullet list, and a bullet list is one paragraph, so all
407	seven were `description#3`. Any entry tracing to any criterion cited the same id.
408	Generation 0 had the same collapse over two claims; defining the item well made
409	it worse by putting more content in each paragraph.
410	
411	### Pass 4
412	
413	**This pass broke the control item rule, on instruction.** Two findings visible in
414	the control item were resolved in `human-work-item` rather than only recorded:
415	
416	1. A finding bundled three undefined cases into one line, against the stated rule
417	   that one finding takes one answer. The rule was a prose aside inside step 3 and
418	   did not hold. It is now a test on the answer rather than on the sentence, with
419	   a red flag beside it.
420	2. "Nothing states what must keep working" appeared in earlier runs and not in
421	   this one. It was only reachable through the `missing` lens's general wording.
422	   That lens now names the four things absent more often than present, so finding
423	   them does not depend on thinking of them.
424	
425	**The consequence, stated so it is not lost.** The control item exists to detect
426	the skills being fitted to the item under test, and it works only while nothing
427	is changed on its account. For these two behaviours it is no longer a control —
428	it cannot now show whether the fix generalises, because the fix was written
429	against it.
430	
431	**Both fixes were then verified against #156**, which neither skill had ever been
432	run on and which nothing has been changed on account of. That is what the
433	compromised control could no longer answer.
434	
435	On #156 the run produced twelve findings and said so — "twelve findings, each
436	needing its own answer". The partial-failure case and the already-claimed case
437	came out as two findings rather than one, which is the split the old behaviour
438	would not have made. "Nothing is said about what must keep working" appeared by
439	name, along with the out-of-scope and failure-case items the `missing` lens now
440	lists. The fourth listed item, a number for a vague quantity, correctly did not
441	appear: #156 uses no such word.
442	
443	#156 carries no labels, so it also exercised the fallback. Citations came out as
444	"the Goal line", "description, sentence 2", "title" — readable, and no worse than
445	labels would have been on an item this short.
446	
447	So the fixes generalise on the evidence rather than on the argument. The verified
448	finding stands, and the control item remains compromised for these two behaviours
449	even though the fixes turned out to be sound: it cannot demonstrate that, and
450	#156 had to.
451	
452	Proposed and not acted on: make #156 the control item. It is real rather than
453	synthetic, it fails by omission the way this repository's items actually do, and
454	nothing has been tuned against it.
455	
456	### Pass 5
457	
458	Four findings against `human-work-item`, all from watching it run rather than from
459	reading it.
460	
461	1. **No stopping rule and no triage.** `agent-work-item` step 9 has one; this
462	   skill had none, so every finding read as blocking. The #156 run announced
463	   "Question 1 of 12", which is not a workflow anyone finishes — on a skill whose
464	   subject is that people run out of patience. Findings are now split into
465	   blocking (`contradicted`, `conflict`, missing goal) and everything else, and
466	   there is a "When it is done" section that ends refinement on a condition
467	   rather than on running out of findings.
468	2. **Step 3 cited positions for items that carry labels.** Step 5 was taught to
469	   write `Problem`, `Goal`, `AC1` in pass 3 and step 3 was not, so the skill
470	   produced labelled items and then cited paragraph numbers in them.
471	3. **Every run opened with a sentence explaining its own procedure** — "findings
472	   first, because a rewrite now would carry my guesses". Four runs out of four.
473	   The wording rules banned flourish in general and did not catch this shape.
474	4. **Placeholder detection needed a question asked first.** Counting the findings
475	   is free and catches the same thing earlier. More than about eight on a short
476	   item means it was never defined or holds more than one thing.
477	
478	Re-run on #156 after the edits: it opened with the finding count, declared the
479	item a placeholder, refused to write acceptance criteria, named one blocking
480	finding out of twelve, asked one question, and produced the decided-so-far and
481	open-questions sections instead of an item. It also declined to ask about two
482	findings it judged the goal would settle, which the split enabled and nothing in
483	the skill teaches directly.
484	
485	One difference that is not an improvement: the title-versus-goal mismatch came out
486	as `implementation-leak` where the previous run called it `conflict`. Both are
487	defensible readings.
488	
489	### Pass 6
490	
491	**Stage 2 ran for the first time.** `docs/passes/pass6/boundary.yaml`, fourteen
492	entries, derived from generation 2. Both lint forms clean: failures empty,
493	warnings `W_NO_FLOOR` only, exempt zero.
494	
495	Stage 1 passed with one non-blocking finding — AC1 says "a person is asked" and
496	never says which person.
497	
498	**The item rewrite had silently invalidated the existing boundary.**
499	`boundary/gh-158.yaml` was authored in an earlier session against generation 0 and
500	cites `description#1`, `#2` and `#3`. After the rewrite all three resolve to
501	nothing. It is superseded rather than edited, and kept.
502	
503	Worse than the citations: six of the item's seven criteria had no obligation in it
504	at all, and five of its nine entries are about a prompt template with double-brace
505	placeholders that the item never mentions. It was derived from a placeholder, so
506	its obligations were invented against a chosen design — which is exactly what
507	`human-work-item` now forbids:
508	
509	> A placeholder does not go to the agent stage. That stage derives obligations
510	> from the goal, and given an undecided goal it will invent them.
511	
512	That rule was written in pass 1 from reasoning. This is the same failure already
513	committed to the repository before the rule existed.
514	
515	Findings:
516	
517	1. **`agent-work-item` step 1 is ambiguous about "paragraph".** The earlier author
518	   counted lines, so `description#3` meant the Goal line; counting blank-line
519	   blocks, generation 0 had only two parts and `description#3` named nothing. Two
520	   readers, two answers, one sentence. Bead `domestique-3lf`.
521	2. **`lint-boundary.js` prints `ok` while checks are exempt.** The CLI reported
522	   `ok` on a boundary with three dead citations, and printed no exempt count. The
523	   skill warns about this and the CLI's own output does not, which is modus README
524	   constraint 2 inside modus's own linter: a check that could not run reporting
525	   green. The fix belongs in the CLI, not in the skill.
526	
527	Five findings against the draft, all from step 8 and none catchable by the linter:
528	
529	3. `W-1`'s decision could not be evaluated against its own observation — the
530	   observation collects a population across every item and the decision named one
531	   boundary, with `quantitative: false` foreclosing a threshold. The same shape as
532	   bead `domestique-dpi`.
533	4. `PRES-1` demanded the two step lists be equal where AC6 states a subset, so it
534	   also failed a hand-written boundary needing fewer steps — a case the item
535	   permits.
536	5. AC4's "can be resolved without resolving the others" had no entry. `AC-8`
537	   resolves every blocker at once and passes even where resolution is
538	   order-dependent. Added as `AC-10`.
539	6. AC1's "a person is asked" had no entry. `AC-3` shows only that nothing is
540	   drafted while nothing is answered, which a drafter that never asks anyone also
541	   satisfies. Added as `AC-11`.
542	7. `PRES-1`'s statement stated the containment in the opposite direction from its
543	   own decision. Caught on the second review round.
544	
545	Two review rounds were needed, and the first found four defects in a boundary that
546	had already passed both lint forms. That is the case for step 8 existing: linting
547	is necessary and measures nothing about whether the boundary decides anything.
548	
549	The pass changed what #158 is. The item says "draft the boundary from the
550	ticket"; the input is in fact the output of `agent-work-item`. That is the first
551	`contradicted` finding this process has produced, and it moved the surface — one
552	draft acceptance criterion belonged to stage 1 rather than to the drafter and was
553	removed.
554	
555	Findings against `human-work-item`, both fixed:
556	
557	1. No verdict existed for an item asserting something that is not so. The six
558	   lenses cover absence, internal contradiction, ordering and implementation
559	   leak, but not an item wrong about its own subject. `contradicted` is now the
560	   highest verdict, with a required correction and a note on whether the
561	   correction changes what gets built. The six lenses are unchanged — this
562	   surfaces in step 4, not in the lens pass, because it needs knowledge from
563	   outside the item.
564	2. The skill guarded against implementation in the item and against the agent
565	   adding it, but not against a format arriving inside the human's own answer.
566	   The blocker format was accepted into a draft criterion for exactly that
567	   reason. Step 4 now says to take the behaviour out and confirm that.
568	
569	Findings against this document, all fixed:
570	
571	3. The chain diagram omitted a stage. `agent-work-item` does not produce the
572	   boundary in the target architecture; the drafter #158 delivers does. Today the
573	   skill spans both arrows by hand, which is why the omission survived two
574	   passes.
575	4. The fixture was described as fixed. It advances by design — each pass may
576	   write an improved item back to the issue, and that is the bootstrapping
577	   process rather than an accident.
578	5. The staleness check could not distinguish somebody else editing the issue from
579	   a deliberate advance. Generations are kept and matched.
580	6. The control item was described as a precaution. With the item under test no
581	   longer fixed, it is the only thing holding skill quality honest.
582	
583	## Known harness limits
584	
585	**A refinement needs a person, a check does not.** The probe cannot complete
586	stage 1 — see step 2 of the procedure. Where the item actually has to be rewritten
587	and re-approved, that is an interactive session with somebody answering, not a
588	probe run.
589	
590	**The probe declares its environment; it does not inherit one.** Pass 7's stage 2
591	hung past nineteen minutes with 25 seconds of CPU, asleep on a socket. The cause
592	was not the skill: the run had inherited `~/.claude` and booted `n8n-mcp`,
593	`@azure/mcp` and `chrome-devtools-mcp`, two of which resolve `@latest` from the
594	npm registry every run. `--strict-mcp-config` was added and the same run finished
595	in four minutes.
596	
597	That was a wrong diagnosis before it was a right one. The hang was first written
598	down here as the agent over-reading the repository, and `agent-work-item` step 2
599	was bounded on that reasoning. The bound may still be worth having; the evidence
600	offered for it was not evidence.
601	
602	**A `--cwd` run needs a clean tree.** Permissions are open, because
603	`agent-work-item` step 7 lints a boundary file and a skill cannot lint a file it
604	was not allowed to write — under inherited permissions a run got twelve Bash calls
605	through and had Write denied. Git is what protects the tree, so `probe-skill.js`
606	refuses to start a `--cwd` run against uncommitted work and exits 2.
607	
608	**One run is weak evidence.** The probe does one run and no repetition. Two
609	passes disagreeing about the same defect is expected noise, not a finding about
610	either skill.

# The refinement loop

How modus's two skills and one boundary get improved together.

`docs/plugin-evaluation.md` answers whether a skill fires. This answers something
one level up: whether the three artifacts in a chain are good enough, when each
one's ceiling is set by the artifact before it.

## Why the three cannot be improved separately

The chain is:

```
raw item
  → human-work-item    → a refined item a person can read
  → agent-work-item    → criteria an autonomous agent can work from
  → the drafter (#158) → the boundary
  → assessment         → defects

        ^                             |
        |_____ blockers on the item __|
              agent-work-item refuses
```

The back edge is the part that took eight passes to find. Some gaps in a human
item are only visible when something downstream tries to derive obligations from
it and finds it cannot — you do not know what you need until you need it. So the
chain is not one-way: `agent-work-item`'s gate writes one blocker per missing
thing onto the item, and `human-work-item` has a mode for an item that arrives
that way, which resolves what the blockers name and nothing else.

That is the same mechanism #158 specifies for the drafter it describes. The
process building it gets what it is building.

It terminates on a rule rather than on patience: a condition that fails the gate
twice means the answer did not land, and that is a conversation with a person
rather than another lap.

Today `agent-work-item` spans the last two arrows: a person follows the skill and
writes the boundary manifest by hand. The drafter is what #158 delivers, so the
final arrow is the deliverable rather than a stage the loop can run. The loop runs
the stages that exist.

A refined item that never states what must keep working gives the stages below it
nothing to write a preservation entry from. The boundary is then missing that
entry, and the boundary is not what is wrong. Tuning `agent-work-item` against a
weak refined item measures the item, not the skill.

So a pass runs the whole chain and the fixes land wherever the defect was
created.

## The item under test

GitHub #158, "Draft the boundary from the refined criteria". It is the goal and
the fixture at once: completing it requires running the process it describes.
Pass 3 rewrote its title and body, so the placeholder wording that pass 1 and 2
worked against is now only in `docs/passes/pass1/item.json`.

The GitHub issue is the item of record. Beads are derivative — `domestique-3z5`
covers the same goal, and where the two disagree the issue wins. A reader outside
this repository can see the issue; bead ids are hash-suffixed and mean nothing to
them.

### Where the item lives

`docs/passes/passN/item.json` is the GitHub API response as fetched at the start
of pass N, stored verbatim rather than as pasted text. `agent-work-item` step 1
warns that a tracker's UI and its API can return different content for the same
item, and bead `domestique-2no` is open on it, so the fixture is what an adapter
actually receives.

The item advances by design. A pass may write an improved item back to the issue,
and the next pass fetches it again — so the item converges alongside the skills.
This is the bootstrapping period and several changes are expected before the
drafter exists.

There is one number, the pass number. An earlier version of this document kept a
separate generation count and the two did not line up: generations 1 and 2 both
came out of pass 3. The historical files are under `docs/passes/pass1/` and
`docs/passes/pass3/`, which is where they belong.

`modus/evals/158-human-work-item/expected.md` records what was decided, who
decided it, the inferences drawn rather than asked, and the split proposed and not
made. It does not copy the item text — the pass directories hold that, and two
copies would drift.

**An item is never at a fixed point while the skills are still changing.** What
converges is the pair, not the item. A better skill finds more on the same text,
so more findings after a skill edit is the expected result and is evidence the
edit worked.

An earlier version of this document said the opposite — that a pass over an
unchanged item should find nothing. Pass 7 found nine findings on the text passes
4 to 6 had run against, because passes 4 and 5 had improved `human-work-item` in
between. The claim was wrong in its polarity: finding nothing is the exception.

## How a pass runs

Every pass writes into its own directory, so a pass can be re-read after the fact
and compared with the one before it.

```
docs/passes/passN/
  item.json          the issue as fetched at the start of the pass
  stage1-*.txt       what human-work-item said about it
  stage2-*.txt       what agent-work-item said about it
  boundary.yaml      the boundary, where stage 2 produced one
  stage2-review.md   what step 8 found
  notes.md           this session's evaluation of the pass
```

Both skills write there themselves, conditional on the directory existing. The
path is this repository's and not part of either plugin, so outside a checkout
with `docs/passes/` the instruction is inert.

**1. Make the directory and fetch the item.**

```bash
N=7; mkdir -p docs/passes/pass$N
gh issue view 158 --json number,url,title,state,body,labels,comments,author,createdAt,updatedAt \
  | python3 -m json.tool > docs/passes/pass$N/item.json
```

The fetched item is the pass's input. There is no separate generation numbering —
one number, the pass number, and `docs/passes/passN/item.json` is what pass N ran
against.

**2. Stage 1 — `human-work-item`. A check, not a gate.**

```bash
node scripts/probe-skill.js --plugin modus --expect modus:human-work-item \
  --prompt "$(...)" --full > docs/passes/pass$N/stage1-human-work-item.txt
```

It reports whether the current item still generates findings, and which of them
block. The pass continues either way. Runs in the neutral temporary directory,
because stage 1 reads the item and nothing else.

The probe is one-shot and `human-work-item` stops after one question, so a probe
run reaches its findings and its first question and no further. As a check that
does not matter. It cannot complete a refinement, so do not plan a pass that
expects it to.

**3. Stage 2 — `agent-work-item`. This one gates.**

```bash
node scripts/probe-skill.js --plugin modus --expect modus:agent-work-item \
  --cwd "$(pwd)" --prompt "$(...)" --full > docs/passes/pass$N/stage2-agent-work-item.txt
```

`--cwd` is required. Step 2 of that skill reads the repository to find what the
item does not say, and the probe's default temporary directory has nothing in it.

No boundary can be produced without complete criteria from this stage, so this is
where a pass stops. Its own step 1b refuses an item missing an outcome, a
falsifiable criterion per obligation, what must keep working, or what is out of
scope — and says which is absent rather than drafting a partial boundary.

**3b. Route every stage-1 finding.** Stage 1 does not gate, and that is not the
same as its output being advisory. Each finding goes to exactly one place, by the
attribution rule below:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| the item is wrong or incomplete | fix the item, and the next pass fetches it |
| the skill missed it before and finds it now | nothing to fix — the skill edit worked |
| the skill should have found it and did not | fix the skill |
| nobody has decided it | record it, with a name against it |

A finding left in a transcript is a finding nobody acts on. Pass 7 produced nine
and this step did not exist, so all nine sat in a file.

**4. Evaluate the pass.** Read all of it and look for what is missing. Write the
result to `notes.md` in the pass directory, and add a row to the pass record at
the end of this document. This step is a person and a session, not a script.

## The assessment

One check, and it is the one `agent-work-item`'s own review questions do not ask.

**Does the boundary name what the item does not.** The value is in the consumer,
the constant, or the missing test the item never mentions. A boundary that
restates the item in manifest form lints clean and saves nobody anything. This is
AC-9 in `boundary/agent-work-item-skill.yaml`.

Two other checks used to live here — whether a fresh reader can state what must be
true, and whether every `decision` can be false. Both are already in the skill, as
step 9 and as one of step 8's two questions, so they were a second copy that could
drift. Run the skill's steps and read what step 8 returned.

They were also declared to "run every pass", which was never true of any pass:
passes 1 to 5 never reached stage 2, and pass 6 was the first to produce a
boundary at all.

## The attribution rule

A defect in the boundary does not mean the boundary is what to fix.

**Fix at the earliest stage whose output already contained the defect.**

Read backwards from the defect:

| The defect is already visible in | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| the raw item, and the refined item did not resolve it | `human-work-item` |
| the refined item, absent from the raw item | `human-work-item` |
| the boundary, absent from the refined item | `agent-work-item` |
| nothing upstream, and both skills were followed as written | the boundary draft |
| the raw item, and the human answered "not decided" | nothing — the item is a placeholder |
| the raw item, and the human says the item is wrong about its own subject | the item itself — a `contradicted` finding, which may change what gets built |

Three consequences worth stating, because all three are easy to get wrong:

- A defect present in the refined item **and** the boundary belongs to
  `human-work-item`. It will also look like an `agent-work-item` defect. It is
  not one.
- A skill that was not followed is not a skill defect until you have checked
  whether it *could* be followed. If the instruction was clear and got skipped,
  that is a compliance failure and the fix is bulletproofing, not new content.
  See `superpowers:writing-skills` on matching the form to the failure.
- A recorded open question is not a defect. A skill refusing to guess is the
  skill working. Attribute a defect only where a skill could have resolved
  something and did not.

## The control item

A second work item that runs through the flow every pass, and that the skills are
never edited because of. Its only job is to catch one failure: the skills getting
fitted to #158 instead of to work items in general.

Without it, each pass adds instructions that happen to help #158. The skills
improve on #158 and get no better — possibly worse — on anything else. #158's own
results cannot show that, because #158 is improving the whole time.

The item: the CSV export ticket in
`modus/evals/human-work-item-resolves-before-rewriting/prompt.md`. Synthetic,
written to carry one defect per lens.

Read its result every pass. Change nothing on its account. If it degrades while
#158 improves, the last edit fitted #158.

Once the item under test advances each pass, this is the only thing left holding
skill quality honest. A better boundary can come from a better item as easily as
from a better skill, and the attribution rule covers defects rather than
improvements. This item is not a precaution any more.

**What this control item cannot detect.** It fails by contradiction and runs about
twice the length of a real issue here. The five open issues are 273 to 460
characters, carry a labelled Problem and Goal, and fail by omission instead. So
this item can show the skills being fitted to #158's subject. It cannot show them
being fitted to long contradictory tickets and losing the terse-omission case,
which is the failure this repository's own items actually have. Swapping in a
real issue — #156 is the furthest from #158 in subject — is the fix if that
becomes a live worry.

## These passes are pre-freeze

`agent-work-item` step 10 says a frozen boundary is the standard and is not
edited. This loop re-drafts the boundary every pass, so no boundary produced by a
pass is frozen. Each carries the marker:

```
# NOT FROZEN. Pass N of the refinement loop.
```

The freeze happens once, after the loop stops, on the boundary that a human
approves. Editing a frozen boundary because a later pass disagreed with it is the
failure modus exists to prevent.

## Proposed and unresolved

Proposals a pass makes and nobody has settled. Without this they are re-proposed
from scratch every pass, and the fact that they keep coming back is lost.

| Proposal | Raised | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| split #158 in two | pass 6 along AC3/AC4, pass 7 along AC6/AC7 | unresolved. Two passes proposed different lines, which is itself evidence the item holds more than one goal and that nobody can say where the seam is |
| make #156 the control item | pass 4 | unresolved. The synthetic export ticket is compromised for two behaviours after pass 4 drove edits from it |
| reduce the two human touchpoints | pass 3 | deferred by decision, blocked on measuring what review costs |

A proposal that recurs with a different shape each time is not the same proposal
twice. It is a signal that the question is wrong, or that the item is too broad to
answer it.

## When the loop stops

Three conditions, and the third is the one that makes the other two mean
anything:

- The boundary names what the item does not.
- The control item did not degrade.
- **Neither the skills nor the item changed since the previous pass, and stage 1
  still finds nothing new.**

The third condition is why reaching a fixed point takes a deliberate act. While
skills keep improving, each pass finds more on the same item, and "more findings"
is indistinguishable from "the item got worse" if nothing was held still. Ending
the loop means choosing one pass in which nothing is edited, and seeing what a
frozen pair finds.

An earlier version required "no change to either skill", which no pass can satisfy
while the loop is doing its job — the loop's whole design is that skills improve
every pass.

## When the loop is blocked

Not the same as stopping. The loop is blocked when every remaining open question
needs evidence nobody has. No number of passes closes it, and further passes
produce invented answers.

**Try to unblock before declaring it.** An undecided question is not the only
thing standing in the way — the item's scope is also in play, and scope is
decidable today because it is a human's call rather than a measurement. See
Unblocking a placeholder in `human-work-item`: move the decision out of the item,
separate motivation from requirement, or replace the unmeasurable measure with an
observable one.

Pass 1 declared #158 blocked on two questions. Pass 2 unblocked both without
answering either. Declaring blocked before trying those three moves costs a pass
and produces nothing.

Blocked is still a real state and worth reporting when it holds. Name the
questions, name what would answer each, and hold the loop until that evidence
exists.

## Pass record

One row per pass, appended to this file.

| Pass | Findings | Attributed to | Control item |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 5 | `human-work-item` 4, this document 1 | unchanged |
| 2 | 4 | `human-work-item` 2, #158 itself 2 | unchanged |
| 3 | 8 | `human-work-item` 2, this document 4, #158 itself 2 | 8 findings against 10 |
| 4 | 3 | `human-work-item` 2, both skills 1 | **used to drive edits — see below** |
| 5 | 4 | `human-work-item` 4 | n/a — verified on #156 |
| 6 | 7 | `agent-work-item` 1, `lint-boundary.js` 1, the draft 5 | not re-run |

### Pass 1

Stage 1 only. #158 is a placeholder: the human's role once the feature ships, and
the number that decides "scales", are both undecided rather than unwritten.
Stages 2 and 3 did not run.

Findings against `human-work-item`:

1. Step 4 gave a form for conflicts only. With no form for a missing
   requirement, the run offered the human a menu of invented answers — and named
   a linter, a manifest schema and a fixture corpus inside it, which is
   implementation inside a question about the WHAT.
2. No red flag against offering that menu.
3. The wording rules banned metaphor but not unexplained vocabulary, so
   "preservation obligation" and "held-out item" reached the human unexplained.
4. No notion of a placeholder. The skill assumed refinement throughout, and its
   Out of scope excluded "creating a work item from nothing" — excluding its own
   common case.

Finding against this document: the attribution table had no row for an answer of
"not decided", so a correctly recorded open question read as a `human-work-item`
defect. Fixed above.

All five are fixed.

### Pass 2

Stage 1. #158 was unblocked without answering either question from pass 1, using
two of the three moves in Unblocking a placeholder: the human-involvement
decision moved out of the item into a separate one, and "doesn't scale" was
reclassified from requirement to motivation. The measure was then replaced with
an observable one — a reviewer names no entry they had to write themselves.

#158 is defined and awaiting approval. It does not reach `expected.md` until then.

Findings against `human-work-item`, both fixed:

1. "Wait for approval before writing it anywhere" banned the per-pass working
   draft this document requires, so a rejected draft would never be written and
   the comparison would be lost. Step 8 now gates the record rather than the
   notes.
2. The acceptance-criteria test said a bullet needing judgment fails but named no
   forms, and a draft bullet used "approves" — which `boundary-prose.md` rejects
   as a state of mind. The three failing forms are now named with replacements.

Findings against #158, carried to its open questions rather than fixed here:

- A recorded blocker is not required to name what is wrong. A blocker reading
  "rejected" cannot be resolved.
- No outcome after a blocker is resolved: whether drafting resumes on its own or
  has to be re-requested.

Both came out of step 7, the second lens pass over the rewrite, on the first item
that step has ever run against.

### Pass 3

Complete. #158 was rewritten and approved, and the title and body were written
back to the issue. The fixture was re-captured as generation 1 and generation 0
kept. Generation 2 followed, adding citation labels without changing wording.

Both skills learned the label scheme. `human-work-item` step 5 labels every
separately falsifiable claim; `agent-work-item` step 1 cites a label where the
item carries one and falls back to `<field>#<n>` where it does not. The fallback
matters — #156, #157 and the control item carry no labels and still work.

The label change came from a defect the definition itself created. Generation 1
put seven criteria in one bullet list, and a bullet list is one paragraph, so all
seven were `description#3`. Any entry tracing to any criterion cited the same id.
Generation 0 had the same collapse over two claims; defining the item well made
it worse by putting more content in each paragraph.

### Pass 4

**This pass broke the control item rule, on instruction.** Two findings visible in
the control item were resolved in `human-work-item` rather than only recorded:

1. A finding bundled three undefined cases into one line, against the stated rule
   that one finding takes one answer. The rule was a prose aside inside step 3 and
   did not hold. It is now a test on the answer rather than on the sentence, with
   a red flag beside it.
2. "Nothing states what must keep working" appeared in earlier runs and not in
   this one. It was only reachable through the `missing` lens's general wording.
   That lens now names the four things absent more often than present, so finding
   them does not depend on thinking of them.

**The consequence, stated so it is not lost.** The control item exists to detect
the skills being fitted to the item under test, and it works only while nothing
is changed on its account. For these two behaviours it is no longer a control —
it cannot now show whether the fix generalises, because the fix was written
against it.

**Both fixes were then verified against #156**, which neither skill had ever been
run on and which nothing has been changed on account of. That is what the
compromised control could no longer answer.

On #156 the run produced twelve findings and said so — "twelve findings, each
needing its own answer". The partial-failure case and the already-claimed case
came out as two findings rather than one, which is the split the old behaviour
would not have made. "Nothing is said about what must keep working" appeared by
name, along with the out-of-scope and failure-case items the `missing` lens now
lists. The fourth listed item, a number for a vague quantity, correctly did not
appear: #156 uses no such word.

#156 carries no labels, so it also exercised the fallback. Citations came out as
"the Goal line", "description, sentence 2", "title" — readable, and no worse than
labels would have been on an item this short.

So the fixes generalise on the evidence rather than on the argument. The verified
finding stands, and the control item remains compromised for these two behaviours
even though the fixes turned out to be sound: it cannot demonstrate that, and
#156 had to.

Proposed and not acted on: make #156 the control item. It is real rather than
synthetic, it fails by omission the way this repository's items actually do, and
nothing has been tuned against it.

### Pass 5

Four findings against `human-work-item`, all from watching it run rather than from
reading it.

1. **No stopping rule and no triage.** `agent-work-item` step 9 has one; this
   skill had none, so every finding read as blocking. The #156 run announced
   "Question 1 of 12", which is not a workflow anyone finishes — on a skill whose
   subject is that people run out of patience. Findings are now split into
   blocking (`contradicted`, `conflict`, missing goal) and everything else, and
   there is a "When it is done" section that ends refinement on a condition
   rather than on running out of findings.
2. **Step 3 cited positions for items that carry labels.** Step 5 was taught to
   write `Problem`, `Goal`, `AC1` in pass 3 and step 3 was not, so the skill
   produced labelled items and then cited paragraph numbers in them.
3. **Every run opened with a sentence explaining its own procedure** — "findings
   first, because a rewrite now would carry my guesses". Four runs out of four.
   The wording rules banned flourish in general and did not catch this shape.
4. **Placeholder detection needed a question asked first.** Counting the findings
   is free and catches the same thing earlier. More than about eight on a short
   item means it was never defined or holds more than one thing.

Re-run on #156 after the edits: it opened with the finding count, declared the
item a placeholder, refused to write acceptance criteria, named one blocking
finding out of twelve, asked one question, and produced the decided-so-far and
open-questions sections instead of an item. It also declined to ask about two
findings it judged the goal would settle, which the split enabled and nothing in
the skill teaches directly.

One difference that is not an improvement: the title-versus-goal mismatch came out
as `implementation-leak` where the previous run called it `conflict`. Both are
defensible readings.

### Pass 6

**Stage 2 ran for the first time.** `docs/passes/pass6/boundary.yaml`, fourteen
entries, derived from generation 2. Both lint forms clean: failures empty,
warnings `W_NO_FLOOR` only, exempt zero.

Stage 1 passed with one non-blocking finding — AC1 says "a person is asked" and
never says which person.

**The item rewrite had silently invalidated the existing boundary.**
`boundary/gh-158.yaml` was authored in an earlier session against generation 0 and
cites `description#1`, `#2` and `#3`. After the rewrite all three resolve to
nothing. It is superseded rather than edited, and kept.

Worse than the citations: six of the item's seven criteria had no obligation in it
at all, and five of its nine entries are about a prompt template with double-brace
placeholders that the item never mentions. It was derived from a placeholder, so
its obligations were invented against a chosen design — which is exactly what
`human-work-item` now forbids:

> A placeholder does not go to the agent stage. That stage derives obligations
> from the goal, and given an undecided goal it will invent them.

That rule was written in pass 1 from reasoning. This is the same failure already
committed to the repository before the rule existed.

Findings:

1. **`agent-work-item` step 1 is ambiguous about "paragraph".** The earlier author
   counted lines, so `description#3` meant the Goal line; counting blank-line
   blocks, generation 0 had only two parts and `description#3` named nothing. Two
   readers, two answers, one sentence. Bead `domestique-3lf`.
2. **`lint-boundary.js` prints `ok` while checks are exempt.** The CLI reported
   `ok` on a boundary with three dead citations, and printed no exempt count. The
   skill warns about this and the CLI's own output does not, which is modus README
   constraint 2 inside modus's own linter: a check that could not run reporting
   green. The fix belongs in the CLI, not in the skill.

Five findings against the draft, all from step 8 and none catchable by the linter:

3. `W-1`'s decision could not be evaluated against its own observation — the
   observation collects a population across every item and the decision named one
   boundary, with `quantitative: false` foreclosing a threshold. The same shape as
   bead `domestique-dpi`.
4. `PRES-1` demanded the two step lists be equal where AC6 states a subset, so it
   also failed a hand-written boundary needing fewer steps — a case the item
   permits.
5. AC4's "can be resolved without resolving the others" had no entry. `AC-8`
   resolves every blocker at once and passes even where resolution is
   order-dependent. Added as `AC-10`.
6. AC1's "a person is asked" had no entry. `AC-3` shows only that nothing is
   drafted while nothing is answered, which a drafter that never asks anyone also
   satisfies. Added as `AC-11`.
7. `PRES-1`'s statement stated the containment in the opposite direction from its
   own decision. Caught on the second review round.

Two review rounds were needed, and the first found four defects in a boundary that
had already passed both lint forms. That is the case for step 8 existing: linting
is necessary and measures nothing about whether the boundary decides anything.

The pass changed what #158 is. The item says "draft the boundary from the
ticket"; the input is in fact the output of `agent-work-item`. That is the first
`contradicted` finding this process has produced, and it moved the surface — one
draft acceptance criterion belonged to stage 1 rather than to the drafter and was
removed.

Findings against `human-work-item`, both fixed:

1. No verdict existed for an item asserting something that is not so. The six
   lenses cover absence, internal contradiction, ordering and implementation
   leak, but not an item wrong about its own subject. `contradicted` is now the
   highest verdict, with a required correction and a note on whether the
   correction changes what gets built. The six lenses are unchanged — this
   surfaces in step 4, not in the lens pass, because it needs knowledge from
   outside the item.
2. The skill guarded against implementation in the item and against the agent
   adding it, but not against a format arriving inside the human's own answer.
   The blocker format was accepted into a draft criterion for exactly that
   reason. Step 4 now says to take the behaviour out and confirm that.

Findings against this document, all fixed:

3. The chain diagram omitted a stage. `agent-work-item` does not produce the
   boundary in the target architecture; the drafter #158 delivers does. Today the
   skill spans both arrows by hand, which is why the omission survived two
   passes.
4. The fixture was described as fixed. It advances by design — each pass may
   write an improved item back to the issue, and that is the bootstrapping
   process rather than an accident.
5. The staleness check could not distinguish somebody else editing the issue from
   a deliberate advance. Generations are kept and matched.
6. The control item was described as a precaution. With the item under test no
   longer fixed, it is the only thing holding skill quality honest.

## Known harness limits

**A refinement needs a person, a check does not.** The probe cannot complete
stage 1 — see step 2 of the procedure. Where the item actually has to be rewritten
and re-approved, that is an interactive session with somebody answering, not a
probe run.

**The probe declares its environment; it does not inherit one.** Pass 7's stage 2
hung past nineteen minutes with 25 seconds of CPU, asleep on a socket. The cause
was not the skill: the run had inherited `~/.claude` and booted `n8n-mcp`,
`@azure/mcp` and `chrome-devtools-mcp`, two of which resolve `@latest` from the
npm registry every run. `--strict-mcp-config` was added and the same run finished
in four minutes.

That was a wrong diagnosis before it was a right one. The hang was first written
down here as the agent over-reading the repository, and `agent-work-item` step 2
was bounded on that reasoning. The bound may still be worth having; the evidence
offered for it was not evidence.

**A `--cwd` run needs a clean tree.** Permissions are open, because
`agent-work-item` step 7 lints a boundary file and a skill cannot lint a file it
was not allowed to write — under inherited permissions a run got twelve Bash calls
through and had Write denied. Git is what protects the tree, so `probe-skill.js`
refuses to start a `--cwd` run against uncommitted work and exits 2.

**One run is weak evidence.** The probe does one run and no repetition. Two
passes disagreeing about the same defect is expected noise, not a finding about
either skill.

# Boundary for gh-158 — "Draft the boundary from the refined criteria".
#
# Pass 8. Item as fetched in docs/passes/pass8/item.json, byte-identical to
# pass 7's. Citations use the labels the item carries — Problem, Goal, AC1..AC7.
#
# Step 1b, the fifth condition. Pass 7's stage 2 refused this item on AC1 and AC5
# as a contradicting pair. That refusal does not hold: AC5 says the redraft happens
# "without anyone being asked again", and the word "again" presupposes one earlier
# ask and forbids a second. AC1 governs entering drafting for an item; AC5 governs
# a redraft inside an item already agreed to. Both hold under that reading, and the
# two alternatives require ignoring "again" (ask every time) or making AC5 dead
# text (re-ask whenever criteria change). A reading that kills another criterion is
# not a live alternative, so no choice between criteria was forced.
#
# The reading is recorded as C3 rather than resolved silently, which is what pass 6
# was faulted for: its AC-8 and AC-11 asserted the same reading and nothing in the
# manifest said a reading had been taken.
#
# Entry ids are OB-* rather than AC-*. Pass 6 used AC-1 for an entry about linting
# while the item's AC1 is about consent, and the near-collision made its coverage
# table hard to read. Item criteria are AC1..AC7 throughout; entries never are.
#
# Round one of step 8 found no unevaluable decision and two blocking questions,
# one of them a real defect: the line between derivable and underivable criteria
# was undrawn while six obligations hung off it. C11 and OB-6 are the fix. See
# stage2-review.md. Round two found OB-2 true by construction and the blocker
# resolution condition undefined; C12 and the rewritten OB-2 are the fix.
#
# NOT FROZEN. No human approval recorded. Step 10 is a person's, not this run's.
schema_version: 1
tracker: github-issues
item: gh-158
registry_revision: "none"
# No registry/invariants.yaml exists in this repository, so the floor is empty and
# W_NO_FLOOR fires. Recorded rather than papered over: every obligation below was
# authored for this item.
registry_selections: []
mandates: [correctness, usability]
non_goals:
  - "reducing how much a person reviews — a separate item, blocked on measuring what review costs"
  - "the boundary manifest's shape; it may change to suit the agent stage and this item neither requires nor prevents that"
  - "producing the refined criteria — that is the upstream stage"
  - "approving or freezing on a person's behalf"

    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"

    verifier: independent_review
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [completeness]
    traces: [C6]
    observation: "give the drafted boundary and the item to a reviewer; ask which entries they had to write themselves"
    decision: "the returned list is empty"
    quantitative: false
  - id: OB-6
    # OB-5's falsification guard. A static, well-formed, gh-158-shaped manifest
    # that ignores its input satisfies every mechanical entry here; a reviewer
    # might or might not catch it. This entry catches it every time.
    statement: "a drafted boundary differs when the criteria it was drafted from differ"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [completeness]
    traces: [C6]
    observation: "draft from the criteria, change the text of one criterion, draft again, compare the two files"
    decision: "the goal, the problem, or one claim differs between the two"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"
  - id: OB-7
    statement: "criteria missing more than one derivation condition record one blocker per missing thing"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [refusal]
    traces: [C7, C13]
    observation: "run the drafter on criteria missing more than one derivation condition; count the blockers it records"
    decision: "the blocker count equals the number of missing conditions"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"

    statement: "a run that records blockers writes no boundary file"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [refusal]
    traces: [C7]
    observation: "run the drafter on criteria missing a derivation condition; list the boundary files for the item"
    decision: "no boundary file exists for the item"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"
  - id: OB-9
    statement: "each recorded blocker names the missing criterion or the undecided question"
    verifier: independent_review
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [refusal]
    traces: [C8, CPL-2]
    observation: "give a reviewer the criteria and every blocker recorded from them; ask which blockers name neither"
    decision: "the returned list is empty"

    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [refusal]

    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"

    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [refusal]
    traces: [C10, C14]
    observation: "resolve every blocker on a refused item, re-run the drafter, list the boundary files"
    decision: "a boundary file for the item exists"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"
  - id: OB-12

    # be equal also fails a hand-written boundary that needs fewer steps, which
    # the item permits — pass 6's PRES-1 did exactly that.
    statement: "freezing a hand-written boundary requires no step that freezing a drafted boundary does not require"
    verifier: independent_review
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [preservation]
    traces: [C11, CPL-1]
    observation: "give the freeze procedure and both kinds of boundary to a reviewer; ask which steps each kind requires"
    decision: "the hand-written step list is a subset of the drafted one"
    quantitative: false

    # top-level field from a copy of one of these files and the test must report a
    # failure. Without that probe, pass on base and pass on head is satisfied by
    # asserting nothing.
    statement: "every boundary file already in the repository lints with no failure"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [preservation]
    traces: [C11, CPL-6]
    observation: "run the boundary linter over every file in the repository's boundary directory"
    decision: "no file reports a failure"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: preservation
    baseline: pass
  - id: OB-14
    # "recorded approval by a person" is read as attributable to a named person. A
    # bare recorded flag also satisfies the words and a script can set it, which
    # would discharge AC7 with no person involved.
    statement: "a frozen boundary carries an approval attributable to a named person"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [approval]
    traces: [C12, CPL-4]
    observation: "freeze a boundary, then read the freeze record written for it"
    decision: "the record names the person who approved"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"
  - id: OB-15
    # OB-14's guard, and the whole content of AC7's second sentence. Without it,
    # OB-14 is satisfied by a record that points at the merge approver. The bundle
    # digest is the repository's own freeze mechanism, carried by CPL-4: a merge
    # approval cannot be inside a bundle frozen before the merge.
    statement: "the approval a frozen boundary carries is part of the frozen bundle"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [approval]
    traces: [C12]
    observation: "compute the bundle digest for a frozen boundary; list the assets that digest covers"
    decision: "the approval record is one of the covered assets"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"
  - id: OB-16
    statement: "a drafted boundary reports no failure from the boundary linter"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [validity]
    traces: [CPL-3]
    observation: "lint the drafted boundary with the item's addressable part list supplied"
    decision: "the failure list is empty"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"
  - id: OB-17
    # Omitting the part list makes every item_locator check exempt itself, and the
    # draft then lints clean with citations that point at nothing. That is how
    # boundary/gh-158.yaml kept three dead citations and still printed ok.
    statement: "every linter check has a domain when a drafted boundary is linted"
    verifier: mechanical
    verification_stage: pre_merge
    obligation: must
    mandate: [validity]
    traces: [CPL-3]
    observation: "lint the drafted boundary with the item's part list supplied; read the exempt checks"
    decision: "no check is recorded exempt"
    quantitative: false
    test_role: change
    baseline: expected_error
    error_code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
    error_pattern: "Cannot find module"
